source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Rama thus heard that supremely auspicious song for many days, accompanied by sages, kings, and monkeys.
verses.2: Having recognized Kusha and Lava as Sita's sons through that song, Rama, by his own intention, called messengers of pure conduct and spoke words in the midst of that assembly.
verses.3: He instructed them, "Go from here to the presence of the revered one (Valmiki) and speak my words."
verses.4: In the midst of the assembly, Rama spoke, saying that if Sita is of pure conduct or free from sin, she should perform her purification here, having obtained the great sage's permission.
verses.5: Having understood the wish of the sage and the thought in Sita's mind, who desires to give proof, then quickly report it to me.
verses.6: Let Maithili, Janaka's daughter, perform an oath tomorrow morning in the midst of the assembly for her own purification and indeed for mine.
verses.7: Having heard this most wonderful speech of Rama, the messengers went forth to the hermitage where the foremost among sages, Valmiki, resided.
verses.8: Having bowed down to the great soul, who was shining with immeasurable splendor, they spoke Rama's words, which were both soft and sweet.
verses.9: Having heard their words and understood Rama's intention, the greatly effulgent sage Valmiki then spoke.
verses.10: Let it be so, good fortune to you, as Rama speaks, so will Sita do, for indeed, a husband is the deity of a woman.
verses.11: All the royal messengers, thus addressed by the sage, quickly returned to the greatly powerful Rama and conveyed the sage's words.
verses.12: Then, greatly delighted after hearing the words of the great soul Valmiki, Rama addressed the sages and kings assembled there.
verses.13: O revered sages with your disciples, and O kings with your followers, let all who desire witness Sita's oath.
verses.14: Having heard the words of the great-souled Rama, a great acclamation arose from all the chief sages.
verses.15: The great-souled kings also praised Rama, saying, "O best among men, this is fitting only in you on earth, and not in anyone else."
verses.16: Having thus made the decision for "tomorrow," Rama, the destroyer of enemies, then dismissed all of them.
